title: SE Enablement: Messaging & Demo Practice
summary: Internal enablement session focused on sharpening messaging, competitive positioning, and practicing demo flows. Covered top value props (production-first performance, cost controls, unified runtime), common objections (latency vs cost, on-prem vs hosted), and ran two short demo roleplays with feedback. Agreed follow-ups: update cheat sheet, record golden demo clip, circulate security FAQ for demo talking points.

Avery to update SE cheat sheet with new objection responses by 2026-11-22

transcript:
Header: 2026-11-18 14:00 UTC | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Liam, Sofia, Priya, Ethan, Avery, Jordan, Nina

00:00 Liam: okay thanks everyone for joining, um we're gonna run through messaging and then do two short demo roleplays, keep it tight 60 minutes, cool?
00:18 Sofia: yeah i can start with the messaging pillars, so we want to keep it simple — production first, cost controls, and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and then hit the differentiate points like routing, KV cache, and compile-time kernel selection
00:41 Priya: quick note, when folks ask about latency vs cost we should say "predictable SLOs with dedicated pools" then add how optimize suggests batching/caching to lower unit cost
01:03 Ethan: i keep hearing "predictable" in the deck, but can we tighten the phrase? maybe "predictable latency and unit economics" sounds a bit cleaner, but not sure
01:22 Sofia: agreed slight tweak — also watch out for jargon in customer comms like kv-cache or kvcache, some reps mispronounce it, i say "prefix cache" in the demo
01:40 Jordan: question — how do we frame private on-prem for compliance-first customers without scaring them with complexity?
01:55 Priya: emphasize private control plane option, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and the turnkey on-prem package. then offer a pilot with limited scope to reduce risk
02:18 Liam: good. ok competitive callouts: against OpenAI we emphasize cost/control and deployment modes; against Anthropic highlight runtime perf and observability; for CompetitorX call out lack of unified feature parity and poor autoscaling
02:45 Nina: note — sometimes in calls people say "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated" — small but it matters for consistency, try to use full product names
03:05 Sofia: let's move into demo practice, roleplay 1: ae opens, se demos latency chart and routing config, ae wraps with pricing ask and next steps
03:30 Roleplay start
03:30 Jordan (AE): hi thanks for your time, quick background — can you share current inference pain points?
03:48 Avery (mock-customer): yeah, main issues are peaky traffic and token cost. latency spikes during peak hours and we have compliance constraints
04:05 Priya (SE): totally, we usually ask about sequence lengths and typical qps; for peaky workloads Dedicated with burst capacity often helps, plus automatic prefix caching can reduce repeated token work
04:28 Jordan: and if they ask about model quality regression when quantizing?
04:35 Priya: right, we recommend model-specific quant profiles and run pre-flight evals. also Redwood Optimize suggests quant settings by workload and we have rollback/rollout policies
04:50 Jordan: sound good — can we show the latency dashboard now?
05:02 Sofia: pulling up demo, heads up demo uses a sandbox dataset, numbers are demo only... 05:20] Sofia: (screen) here's per-route latency, token cost per route, and a trace for a sample request showing KV hit on prefix cache
05:38 Jordan: callout the trace: show where fallback to cheaper model happened during a capacity spike
05:55 Sofia: yes, that trace shows smart routing — request routed to a compatible cheaper variant, fallback preserved correctness, kept service online
06:15 Avery: objection roleplay: customer asks about SOC 2 and data residency
06:23 Priya: answer: we're SOC 2 ready, have audit logs and fine-grained RBAC, and for data residency we offer private deployments in the customer's region or on-prem option; reference security FAQ (i'll paste link after)
06:45 Jordan: pricing ask — how do i explain committed Dedicated contracts vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
06:51 Liam: say: hosted for fast time-to-value and variable usage, dedicated for predictable throughput and unit costs; committed gives lower unit pricing and SLA-backed latency/uptime, but needs a consumption forecast
07:12 Sofia: quick transcription glitch — sometimes the auto-transcript writes "kv-cache" as "k v cache" so when we share notes watch that
07:30 Roleplay feedback
07:30 Liam: feedback — Jordan good cadence, but try to pause more after complex sentences, audience needs breathing room. Priya: solid on tech detail, may be too deep on first pass, save deep dive for follow-on
08:02 Nina: can we standardize an "ask" at the end: 1) pilot eval 2) security review 3) pricing/commitment — seems to close deals smoother
08:20 Sofia: yep, and include a success criteria template in the follow-up email: latency p95 target, cost per 1k tokens, and rollout timeline
08:38 Second roleplay start (shorter)
08:40 Liam (AE): opening, hi again quick run-through of use-case, we want to highlight predictable perf and cost-savings
09:02 Avery (customer): i'm worried about integrating with our SSO and audit needs
09:12 Sofia (SE): we support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and integrations with common KMS; plus we provide audit logs with export for SIEM
09:30 Liam: demo show the Console > security page, toggle SSO, show logs — (pause) small hiccup here demo env is a bit slow today, ignore micro-lag
09:50 Sofia: okay moving to competitive frame, quick script: "Compared to X, we offer unified runtime across environments, which means you don't re-implement infra when you go private; plus cost controls like intelligent batching and caching reduce your unit spend"
10:15 Priya: competitor objection — "X claims lower latency" reply: request a benchmark and propose a 48-hour pilot where we run real traces; include our optimize recommendations and runtime tuning
10:40 Jordan: can we add a line about integration effort, like "deployment abstraction reduces lift" — customers want to know how much engineering time to expect
10:52 Sofia: use framing: "one integration to switch models, pin versions, and rollout policies across hosted/dedicated/private" — keeps it concise
11:10 Liam: quick notes on collateral: need an updated one-pager for the field with 3 bullets: Production-first perf, Unified deployment, Cost controls — and an appendix for security and benchmark notes
11:30 Avery: also request a short FAQ for pricing objections and a competitor matrix with quick rebuttals
11:45 Nina: tiny language ask: avoid 'we're cheaper' say 'lower unit cost for comparable performance' — more defensible
12:02 Sofia: demo hiccup during recording — audio overlapped, so we should do golden demo recording separately, not during a crowded meeting
12:20 Roleplay wrap and recap
12:22 Liam: recap — action items: record golden demo, update cheat sheet, competitor one-pager, benchmark slides. any other asks?
12:35 Jordan: can we get a 3-min script bullet list for AE openings?
12:40 Avery: yes please, will use those in next week training
12:50 Priya: final quick note: when asked about KV cache hits, translate to customer terms — "reduces repeated token compute by caching prefixes" rather than internal lingo
13:12 Liam: ok thanks everyone — we'll close, i'll send notes and link to updated assets
13:22 Sofia: thanks all
13:25 Meeting ended

Notes: transcript contains typical ASR imperfections (misspellings, spacing), speaker labels are best-effort. Demo timestamps approximate. References mentioned: security FAQ (link to internal wiki), competitor one-pager (to be created), golden demo recording (S3 link TBD).
